title: Production Live Resource Proof Repair

repairs.password_writer: New password writes use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 100000 iterations, within the Cloudflare Workers WebCrypto runtime boundary; legacy SHA-256 verification remains compatibility-only and existing PBKDF2 hashes retain their embedded iteration count for verification.
repairs.application_modules: Browser runtime classification now converges legacy domain routes onto the canonical Storefront, Creators, Socials, Financials and I.T. module keys; /admin/users/ resolves to it-platform instead of retired business-administration.
repairs.public_media: Product and Movie historical public-media URLs may recover through the read-only same-origin /api/product-media route using the environment-bound PRODUCT_MEDIA_BUCKET. The route performs bucket.get only and never lists or mutates R2.
repairs.live_resource_proof: The Production live-resource integrity workflow is strengthened to distinguish source/deployment green from actual live Product/Movie/account resource evidence.

validation_followup.evidence: The earlier workflow invoked Wrangler D1 commands without the canonical Cloudflare account context and exited before resource assertions. Subsequent Build 61 read-only diagnostics confirmed Product/Movie rows and account schema remained present while historical media delivery URLs returned 404.
validation_followup.required_repair: Deploy the exact fully-green Build 61 tree through Development and Production, then verify real live account behavior and Product/Movie image bytes without inferring R2 object presence from database metadata.

closure_rule: Build 61 is a runtime and live-resource verification repair. It must pass the exact-head Development source/quality/I.T. proof set, merge that tested head to dev, pass the exact merged-dev four-proof closure and Preview deployment, then only the same exact tree may be promoted to main under the user's explicit authorization. Production is not considered incident-green unless live account behavior and Product/Movie image bytes are actually proven; database image metadata alone is insufficient.
